newsitem.title: USA: Some U.S. pork packers scale back production.
newsitem.headline: Some U.S. pork packers scale back production.

text.p: Some major U.S. pork packing companies are scaling back on production this week due to tight hog supplies and unfavorable market conditions.
ConAgra Inc cut pork production by one hour a day at its three Swift and Co. pork plants Monday and Tuesday, said K.T. Miller, a ConAgra spokeswoman.

She said the cutbacks were based on market conditions and that production schedules for the rest of the week would be reviewed. The plants are in Marshalltown, Iowa; Worthington, Minn.; and Louisville, Ky.
On Monday, IBP Inc announced it was drastically scaling back pork production at two of its Iowa pork plants because of declining hog supplies in Iowa.

Excel Corp., a subsidiary of Cargill Inc, said there had been no changes in pork production at its two operating pork plants. Production hours were increased at the Beardstown, Ill., and Marshall, Mo., plants to compensate for the loss of production from its Ottumwa, Iowa, plant, said Excel spokesman Mark Klein.
A fire in late January temporarily closed the Ottumwa plant. It was scheduled to reopen March 17, said Klein.
A Farmland Industries official said there were no changes in production at its three pork plants this week. The plants are in Crete, Neb.; Denison, Iowa; and Monmouth, Ill.
Officials were unavailable for comment at Smithfield Foods, which operates six pork plants, including two by its subsidiary John Morrell and Co.
